doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: First drum, the basement drum set and daily practice
summary: He got his first drum at nine, then a drum set, and practiced six to eight hours a day in the basement at home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: That’s saying something. Were you a typical bang-on-the-pots-and-pans-in-the-kitchen little kid?

Well kind of. Not so much the pots and pans. I did bang on everything else around the house, and when I was nine years old I talked my mother into buying my first drum. It was an old medium Ludwig parade drum. For those of you who are going to be watching this overseas, it was medium Ludwig. I used to march up and down the street and just bang on that. Then a few years later, after I’d gone through a number of school bands, grade school, junior high, got into high school and then I sort of evolved over to a set, © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

and became very fascinated and enamored with a drum set. I talked her into buying me one of those too. Of course after that I had everything set up in the basement in our house. My mother was working all the time, all day. My grandfather and grandmother were living there with us, and my grandfather had a job which got him out of the house. My grandmother was partially deaf, because I was down in the basement. During the summers or school break I’d be down there 6-8 hours a day practicing. Well I didn’t know any better.
You didn’t know that this wasn’t fun?

Oh, I was having a marvelous time, this was great. I practiced everything. I practiced dynamics, I practiced tempos, I practiced various rhythms — Latin rhythms, dance rhythms — and played along with records.
